chunks.rationale: Read first and top-to-bottom: every visual decision lives here, and docs.html/changelog.html consume it without their own changes, so a regression here breaks three pages. Check the docs section (docs-layout/docs-nav/docs-content/doc-table/callout/lede) against the class list both pages actually use, and confirm the reveal block keeps the no-JS-fully-visible contract.
risks: @property --mx/--my and animation-timeline are Chromium/Safari-17.4+ features; all uses are wrapped so unsupported engines get the static design, but Firefox deserves a manual look (no scroll-driven shot entrance, progress bar stays scaleX(0) — both intended fallbacks).

body::after grain is a fixed full-viewport layer with an SVG turbulence fill — cheap in real browsers, but it defeated chromium-headless-shell's rasterizer in tall-window captures (blank tiles); verified with real Brave headless instead.
.cell-f changed to span 6; if a future cell reuses cell-f expecting span 3 it will go full-width.

chunks.rationale: Second: shows how the CSS is consumed. New markup: .progress bar, .hero-bg aurora/grid, .hero-pill, .grad headline spans, .marquee provider strip, .glow hooks on cards, .pdot/.col-dot status dots, .final-cta. main.js adds pointer glow (--mx/--my), nav.scrolled, sibling reveal stagger; reveal/scroll-spy logic unchanged.
risks: Marquee content is duplicated 4x and aria-hidden; screen readers skip it by design since providers are named in the hero copy.
Pointer glow listeners attach to every .cell/.glow at load — fine at this page size; a much larger bento would want delegation.
Copy changes are minimal but real: provider list moved out of the hero sub into the marquee, and a final CTA was added after the install grid.

chunks.rationale: Last: only cache-bust bumps (style.css v4, main.js v3). No markup changes; verify by skimming the diff, then judge them from the rendered pages.
risks: None beyond the shared-stylesheet coupling noted above.
Visual-only change verified by screenshot at 1440px and 390px plus docs/changelog captures; no automated tests exist for site/.
Firefox/Safari not actually launched — scroll-driven animations degrade to static by design, but that claim rests on the @supports guards, not a live run.
